sections.title: 8. Accreditation and Recognition of Mechanical Engineering in France**

items: When choosing an undergraduate program, engineering accreditation in France is something to consider.

The **Commission des titres d’ingénieur (CTI)** assesses eligible engineering programs and authorizes institutions to award the French *diplôme d’ingénieur*. This is usually associated with five years of tertiary study and a master's level qualification.
Not all mechanical engineering or science undergraduate programs lead to a CTI-accredited engineering diploma however. A bachelor's degree may be a separate three year qualification.
Before enrollment, Students are recommended to:
- Check the exact qualification issued by the institution.
- Check the CTI accreditation in case they want to get a French engineering diploma.
- Check whether the bachelor qualification qualifies for admission to a relevant master program.
- Verify the international degree recognition requirements of the country where you will work.
- Look into any professional registration or licensing requirements for their selected career.

sections.title: 9. Mechanical Engineering UG in France: Salary & Job Opportunities**

items: **Graduates of the Mechanical Engineering program in France** are able to find work in the manufacturing sector, the automotive industries, aerospace, energy, robotics, industrial automation and product development.
Possible professions are:
* - Engineer in mechanical design.
* - Junior Mechanical Engineer
* - Auto-mechanic technician.
* - Engineer of production or manufacturing.
* Design engineer CAD.
* - Quality Control Engineer
* - Maintenance engineer.
* - Automation and robotics specialist.
* - Materials and Testing Technician
* - Analyst of energy systems.
****Salary expectations:**** The salary depends on the qualification, specialization, location, employer, technical skills, and work experience.
Students should look at current job advertisements and salary surveys to determine realistic salary expectations for their chosen career.

sections.title: 10. Documents Required to Study Mechanical Engineering UG in France**

items: Students applying for ****undergraduate Mechanical Engineering in France**** should prepare the following documents based on the requirements of the institution they have selected:
* - Valid passport.
* - Marksheet and certificate of class 10th.
* - Mark sheet and pass certificate of class 12th.
* - Academic transcripts and grading information, as applicable.

* - Statement of purpose or motivation letter.
* - CV, if required.
* - Letters of recommendation, if needed.
* -Filled out college application form.
* - Application fee payment confirmation (if applicable).
* - Certified academic documents translation if necessary.
* - Any other documents required by the university or admissions platform.
After being offered a place, students may also need to provide further documents for **French student visa processing**, financial proof, accommodation and final enrollment.

sections.title: 11. Mechanical engineering in France – Frequently asked questions**

items: **Q1. Can Indian students pursue **undergraduate Mechanical Engineering in France?****
Yes. Indian students meeting the academic, language and admission criteria can apply for eligible bachelor’s and engineering-school programs in France.
Q2. How many years to complete undergraduate Mechanical Engineering in France?**
Typically, a bachelor’s degree takes three years to complete. A typical French engineering-school path usually takes five years after high school, depending on the admission route.
**Q3. Are there Mechanical Engineering courses in France in English?**

Some institutions provide English-taught engineering programs or international study pathways. But a lot of the traditional engineering programs are taught in French. Students are advised to confirm with the school the language of instruction for the courses before applying.
Q4. ** Undergraduate Mechanical Engineering in France: What is the cost?**

Tuition fees vary depending on the institution and the qualification. The published differentiated fee for non-EU students subject to the relevant public-institution rules is €2,902 per year at bachelor’s level for 2026–2027. Tuition may be higher at private engineering schools.
**Q5. What are the required subjects to study Mechanical Engineering in France?**

Admission to undergraduate mechanical engineering often requires important subjects such as mathematics and physics. Some institutions may also require chemistry or other science subjects depending on the program.
